Area and economic statistics

Checked 6 October 2026. Each region shows the latest annual value found in the sources included here, with a separate year and source for each metric. Coverage is incomplete: a missing figure means it has not been verified for this dataset, not that the region has no economic activity.

Coverage

MapRegionsReported areaApprox. mapped areaGDPGDP per capita

All mapped first- and second-level divisions have a statistics section. The dataset also includes the additional districts already present on the China map. Korea includes both South and North Korea.

Area, in km²

Reported area comes from Wikidata entity records and the published Mongolia province table. These figures can have different reference dates and definitions, including land area or total administrative area. A source without a stated date is labeled accordingly.

Where no unambiguous reported area was found, “Mapped area ≈” is calculated from the atlas’s displayed boundary polygons, with interior holes subtracted. This is approximate geometry, not an official land-area measurement. Coastlines, offshore waters, disputed boundaries and later administrative changes can cause differences. No area values are shown in square miles.

GDP and GDP per capita

GDP means nominal gross domestic product or gross regional domestic product at current prices. It is the output of the entire administrative region, not household income, wages, or the urban core alone. GDP per capita uses a published value where available. Japan’s figures are calculated from GDP and the matching-year population in the Cabinet Office prefectural accounts, with that calculation labeled; the newer census population is not used as the denominator.

China’s provincial and prefectural data use Wikipedia compilations of statistical releases, supplemented by dated regional article entries. These are secondary sources and have not all been independently audited against their original government releases. Provincial data are generally 2025 preliminary figures; many prefectural figures remain older. Undated GDP entries are excluded. Matching uses both region and province to distinguish names such as Suzhou, Fuzhou and Yulin.

South Korea’s first-level figures come from the official 2024 preliminary regional-income report, preserving its rounding. Jeonnam–Gwangju shows the sum of the two predecessor regions’ 2024 GDP, explicitly labeled; no combined GDP-per-capita estimate is supplied. A verified second-level GDP series has not yet been included.

Mongolia’s first-level figures come directly from the National Statistics Office’s regional GDP and GDP-per-capita tables, with 2025 values available for all 21 aimags and Ulaanbaatar. Soum GDP and North Korean regional GDP remain unavailable in this dataset. They are not estimated from provincial totals or population shares.

Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan use their own statistical agencies and currencies. Their districts, counties and cities do not inherit the parent region’s GDP. Taiwan’s total GDP and per-capita GDP currently come from different 2026 releases of 2025 figures; this is noted beside the source.

Japan

All 47 prefectures are included. Population uses the 2025 preliminary census as compiled in Wikipedia. GDP uses the Cabinet Office fiscal 2023 release for 42 prefectures, with fiscal 2022 values retained for the remaining five. GDP per capita is calculated using the same-year population series in the Cabinet Office accounts; it is not prefectural income per person. USD conversions use the matching calendar-year average rate. Area values are reported figures from the prefecture table; differing territorial definitions may affect comparisons with mapped boundaries.

Indonesia and the Philippines

All 38 Indonesian provinces and all 82 Philippine provinces have population, reported land area, nominal GDP and published GDP per capita. Country statistics load only when a province is selected. Cities, regencies and Philippine regions do not inherit provincial totals.

Indonesia uses BPS Statistical Yearbook 2026: 2026 midyear population projections based on the 2020 census and official 2025 provincial areas from the Ministry of Home Affairs. Projection counts are rounded to the nearest 100 people in the published table. GDP and GDP per capita use the April 2026 BPS provincial accounts, appendices 1 and 121, with 2025 very preliminary figures. Per-capita GDP uses the economic table’s 2025 population denominator.

The Philippines uses PSA OpenSTAT: 2024 census population as of 1 July 2024, land area based on the LMB/DENR 2019 masterlist, and 2025 provincial GDP and GDP per capita at current prices. Statistical province totals exclude separately reported cities even where atlas geometry includes them. Basilan figures exclude Isabela City, which is reported separately under Region IX. Maguindanao del Norte and del Sur have separate records.

Download Indonesia statistics or Philippine statistics, including source metadata.

Local currency and USD

Each available economic figure is shown in local currency and USD. USD conversions use the World Bank / IMF IFS annual average exchange-rate series for the same year as that metric. This is a market-rate conversion, not purchasing-power parity (PPP), and may differ from the central-parity rate used in some Chinese summary tables. Taiwan’s USD figures are quoted directly from DGBAS. Exact rates and sources can be expanded in the region panel.

Data and attribution

Download the complete statistics dataset and source metadata. Source snapshots and preparation scripts are retained with the website’s source. Wikipedia-derived tables are adapted under CC BY-SA 4.0; Wikidata claims are CC0. Boundary-derived areas retain the atlas’s boundary-source attribution, including OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Government data are attributed to the respective agencies. Retrieval dates describe this snapshot and do not imply every value was published that day.
